recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Adding separate server-type uniqueness rules or a CapabilityStatement extension would go beyond the published FHIR-20398 resolution and would need a new work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-20398 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked for best-practice rules or terminology for different FHIR server setups where canonical URLs, especially StructureDefinition and SearchParameter URLs, might not be unique. The accepted resolution was to add guidance in the canonical section of the references page explaining that url+version and unversioned canonical URL references might not resolve to a single record and that resolution is governed by server policy.
initial_application: Commit 1c4a35dbe293f96f5b95682b627ef541a838ea92 explicitly applied FHIR-20398 by adding the Choosing the right Canonical Reference section to source/references.html. The current source retains that guidance and has since been refined by later canonical-version changes.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread shows why the work group avoided a universal uniqueness rule: validation services, terminology services, repositories, and archives can have different duplicate-canonical behavior. Vocabulary minutes moved the issue to FHIR-I as an implementation issue, and FHIR-I minutes record the Persuasive with Modification vote. Later FHIR-52895 and FHIR-39270 source changes refined the same canonical matching area without removing the FHIR-20398 server-policy guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/references.html flags multiple canonical matches as policy-dependent, describes no-version, partial-version, and full-version duplicate cases, says the specification does not define the server selection algorithm, and names inputs such as version, publication date, status, package metadata, and additional policy knowledge.
